IMPOSSIBLE: engine aborts with 'VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN'. Serial-exact GDN is what makes batch invariance compatible with GDN attention; the two flags are coupled.
arms.harness_defect: run-arm.sh exited 0 with no bench.json despite the engine failing to initialize

arms.change: both off; margin and oneDNN barriers retained
arms.verdict: FASTEST measured at 98.222/98.717 all-25 but NOT reproducible, so it does not count. Acceptance is unchanged. This arm changed both serial-exact GDN and global batch invariance, so the +6.3 tok/s cannot yet be assigned to either variable or to a specific graph break.

arms.hypothesis: if GDN run-to-run nondeterminism were an ordering race, a completion barrier would fix it far cheaper than serializing the recurrence
arms.verdict: The completion barrier does not repair the failure. It costs about 1 tok/s (97.211 vs 98.222), while the divergent prompts and token positions are byte-identical to the no-barrier run -- same 8 reported prompt/token pairs. This rules out a missing end-of-op completion dependency as the explanation; it does not by itself identify GDN reduction order or separate GDN from the simultaneously disabled global batch-invariant policies.

optimization_ladder_20260818.conclusion: Validated best remains 91.926 tok/s at 25/25 self-determinism. The measured 97-98 tok/s arms are not reproducible. Because the fast arm disabled both serial-exact GDN and global batch invariance, the 6.3 tok/s gap and the divergence are not yet causally assigned. A completion barrier reproduced the same divergence, ruling out a simple missing completion dependency. The published factorial diagnostic is required before selecting the next production implementation target.
